provider_if_inherited: Innkeeping software vendor; OTAs; smart lock vendor
implementation_statement: The vendors provide account functions. The owner holds the administrator account in each service; the bookkeeper has a named accounting user. Gaps: the relief innkeeper uses the owner's accounts in SYS-01 and OTA-2; accounts are never reviewed; P07 testing found the lock installer's administrator account still active since 2022 (disabled 2026-07-23).
evidence: SYS-01, OTA-2, and lock app user lists

implementation_statement: The innkeeping software enforces role permissions, including the permission to display full card numbers. Gap: daily work is done in the administrator account, which has that permission. A front desk role without it will be used for daily work and by the relief innkeeper (2026-10-31).
evidence: SYS-01 role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-innkeeper holds every role, including the books. The bookkeeper does the monthly bookkeeping and the Florida sales and tourist development tax returns in the accounting SaaS through its own user account, so payouts and bank records get a second look each month. Card processing stays with the payment facilitator. Gap: the relief innkeeper uses the owner's logins to the innkeeping software and OTA-2, so their actions cannot be told apart.
evidence: Accounting SaaS user list; monthly bookkeeping; SYS-01 and OTA-2 user lists

implementation_statement: The phone locks after 30 seconds with a passcode. Gap: the laptop locks only after 20 minutes and family members know its password. The owner sets a 5-minute lock and stops family use of the laptop (POL-01 9.1) by 2026-09-15.

The owner has had no security training. By 2026-11-30 the owner completes a short course on phishing, OTA impersonation, and payment fraud, and the relief innkeeper gets a one-page briefing; repeated every year.
The innkeeping software logs sign-ins, card number displays, exports, and setting changes for every user. The owner relies on this logging (SOC 2 report, P09).
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; SYS-01 activity log screen

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has ever reviewed the innkeeping activity log, the email sign-in history, the OTA-2 login history, or the lock app access log. Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews all four on the first Monday of each month and notes the review in the security log.

provider_if_inherited: Innkeeping software vendor; email provider; OTAs; smart lock vendor
implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the logs stay with the vendors. The innkeeping software keeps its activity log of sign-ins, card number displays, exports, and setting changes for 12 months on the vendor's platform. The email, OTA sign-in, and lock access logs stay with their vendors. No log is kept only on the shared laptop.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; SYS-01 activity log screen

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls with help from the on-call IT consultant. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the inn, such as the IT consultant, at least every second year. The innkeeping vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report (bridge letter requested 2026-07-22) and the AOCs from the innkeeping vendor and the payment facilitator cover their inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review has not taken place.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; AOCs; P09 review

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 4.6 requires the owner to confirm in writing where card data flows before any change in how cards are taken. POL-01 7.3 requires default passwords on any device to be changed before use, and POL-01 4.3 requires a risk assessment update after any major change. The IT consultant applies a router and lock settings checklist by 2026-09-30. Gap: POL-01 has no change log for settings, and the AI add-on's rate suggestions auto-apply (P10).

The laptop and phone run vendor security defaults with automatic updates. Gaps: the router administrator password is the default and remote management has never been checked; guest Wi-Fi is not a separate network. The IT consultant applies a short router and lock settings checklist by 2026-09-30.
No list of the components that touch card data existed before this plan. Section 9 of the SSP is the first inventory; the reader's serial number is now recorded for P2PE device checks.
evidence: SSP section 9; reader serial number record

implementation_statement: The BIA (P05), the POL-01 contingency section, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gaps: the relief innkeeper's named account, the sealed emergency access envelope, and a relocation arrangement with a nearby inn are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

The innkeeping vendor backs up SYS-01 (inherited; RTO 4 hours and RPO 1 hour in its SOC 2 system description). Owner responsibility: laptop files have no backup, the innkeeping data has never been exported, and the file account keeps no version history.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; laptop and file account review

implementation_statement: The owner and the bookkeeper have their own accounts. Gap: the relief innkeeper signs in as the owner in SYS-01 and OTA-2, so activity cannot be traced to a person. Named account by 2026-10-31.

provider_if_inherited: Accounting SaaS vendor; OTA-1; innkeeping software vendor; email provider; OTA-2
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced by the accounting SaaS and OTA-1. Gap: MFA is available but off for the innkeeping administrator account, email, and OTA-2. The owner turns it on for all three by 2026-09-15 and stores recovery codes offline.

Gaps: passwords are saved in the laptop browser, one password is reused for the innkeeping software and email, the router administrator password is the default, and the house master door code has not changed since 2022. The owner moves to a password manager with unique passphrases by 2026-09-15 and changes the master code every quarter and when a cleaner leaves.

The reservation system compromise runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list that includes the payment facilitator's 24-hour notice line. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the plan has not been walked through (due 2026-09-30).
Paper is shredded with a home cross-cut shredder. Gaps: reservation pad pages with card numbers have never been shredded, and there is no procedure for wiping old phones and laptops.

Keypad locks issue per-reservation codes that expire at checkout (vendor mechanism). The owner's office holds the laptop and the reservation pad and is not locked during the day. Gap: the house master code has not changed since 2022 and former cleaners know it.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every July and after major changes.

AOCs from the innkeeping vendor and the payment facilitator were obtained on 2026-07-22, and the innkeeping vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed (P09). Gaps: no written list of service providers and what each does with card or guest data; the AI add-on terms were never read; the lock installer kept administrator access for four years.

The router blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and the laptop's host firewall is on. Gap: guests and the owner's devices share one network. The router's guest network feature will separate guest Wi-Fi by 2026-09-30.

The innkeeping software, booking engine, and payment services use TLS (inherited), and the reader encrypts card data at the card (P2PE). Gap: card numbers arrive by email on authorization forms and have been typed into the chat assistant.

The vendors encrypt stored card numbers in their vaults (inherited), and the phone is encrypted. Gaps: the laptop has no full-disk encryption (on by 2026-09-15), and card numbers sit in clear text in email and on paper.

provider_if_inherited: Innkeeping software vendor; device OS vendors
implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors patch their services, and automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone. Gap: the router firmware has never been updated.
The operating system's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

No retention rules exist: pad pages, email card forms, ID photos, and guest profiles are kept indefinitely. Planned schedule (POL-01 8.6): no card data or security codes kept after authorization; ID photos no longer taken; guest register kept 2 years (Fla. Stat. 509.101(2)); inactive guest profiles deleted after 3 years.
